record.context_brief: Improved Gelbrich lower bound for elliptical distributions
record.original_question: For elliptical distributions parameterized by mean, covariance, and radial distribution, can one prove an improved Gelbrich-type lower bound for the 2-Wasserstein distance that depends not only on mean and covariance but also on the radial distributions nu_0 and nu_1?

evidence.quote: Can we develop an improved Gelbrich lower bound that involves also ν0 and ν1?

artifact.status_search_result: The classical Gelbrich bound is known to be tight for elliptical distributions with a common density generator and loose otherwise. Existing extensions (e.g., spectral-domain Gelbrich bounds for elliptical processes) address related directions, but a general improved Gelbrich-type lower bound for elliptical distributions involving the radial distributions $\nu_0, \nu_1$ does not appear to be established in the literature surveyed. The problem appears open.

status_evidence.title: The Spectral-Domain W2 Wasserstein Distance for Elliptical Processes and the Spectral-Domain Gelbrich Bound
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a spectral-domain Gelbrich bound; notes that the Gelbrich bound is tight for elliptical distributions with the same density generator and may be loose otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Improvements of the Gelbrich bound that exploit radial/generator information are an active topic, but a sharp form depending on the radial laws is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization: Theory and Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Uses the Gelbrich bound as a tractable lower bound on Wasserstein distance based on means and covariances; discusses tightness for elliptical families with the same generator.
status_evidence.claim: Standard Gelbrich bound depends only on first two moments; improvement using radial distributions is not stated.
